questions.text: How would you describe the genital rash — is it flat (macular), raised (papular), blistering, scaly, or weeping?
questions.purpose: Characterise morphology to narrow the differential between dermatological, STI, and infective causes

questions.text: Have you had unprotected sexual contact or new sexual partners recently?
questions.purpose: STI risk assessment — rash with sexual exposure requires STI screen

questions.text: Is the rash also present on the palms of your hands, soles of your feet, or in your mouth?
questions.purpose: Widespread rash including palms and soles is a classic sign of secondary syphilis

questions.text: Is the rash intensely itchy, particularly at night?
questions.purpose: Nocturnal itch suggests scabies, which frequently involves the genitalia in males

questions.text: Have you recently changed soaps, washing powders, lubricants, or latex products that contact the genital area?
questions.purpose: Contact dermatitis or irritant dermatitis is a common non-infectious cause of genital rash

questions.text: Do you have a known skin condition such as psoriasis or lichen planus elsewhere on your body?
questions.purpose: Pre-existing skin conditions can manifest on the genitalia and require specialist dermatology management
